code_edition.value: 2023 National Electrical Code (NEC) (2024 Phoenix Building Construction Code)
code_edition.quote: On June 18, 2025, the Phoenix City Council approved the adoption of the 2024 Phoenix Building Construction Code (PBCC). The City of Phoenix is transitioning to this updated code with an effective date of August 1, 2025.

who_may_file.conditions: Owner must occupy the building and act as general contractor; per A.R.S. 32-1121.A(5), property may not be for sale or rent within one year after Certificate of Occupancy.
who_may_file.quote: Arizona Licensed Contractors shall be used for all work and shall be listed on the application form and permit unless the owner, who will occupy the building, is acting as the general contractor.

utility.name: Arizona Public Service (APS) and Salt River Project (SRP)

requirements.item: Contact APS for approved service and meter location before upgrading or relocating service
requirements.quote: Prior to service being changed or relocated to supply new or existing load, contact APS. All service entrances being upgraded (increased main breaker ampacity), or relocated must be brought up to current code and specification requirements.

requirements.item: APS sets meter and energizes service only after receiving City electrical clearance
requirements.quote: When APS receives a City or County clearance, APS will set a meter and energize the service.

requirements.item: APS requires online PowerClerk interconnection application and PTO before operating solar or DER
requirements.quote: Installers apply online using our PowerClerk Application.

requirements.item: SRP requires PowerClerk interconnection application and signed Interconnection Agreement before solar installation
requirements.quote: Contractors must submit a complete application package to SRP on behalf of the customer before the system is installed. This ensures that the system configuration is approved by SRP.

open_questions: Full text of Electric Vehicle Chargers – Residential Permitting (TRT/DOC/00311) at https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Documents/TRT/dsd_trt_pdf_00311.pdf is needed to confirm whether existing single-family Level 2 EVSE installations without a service upgrade over 200 amps require plans.

Residential Over the Counter Permits Guideline (TRT/DOC/00366) at https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Documents/TRT/dsd_trt_pdf_00366.pdf lists electric service upgrades not exceeding 200 amps under Express Permits, and Shape PHX Quick Permits issue 200-amp 1-phase upgrades, but a direct official policy quote explicitly stating no plans are required for single-family service upgrades 200 amps or less (and requiring plans above 200 amps) was not retrieved.

No published City of Phoenix policy document was found explicitly stating whether plans are required for a standalone single-family 240 V appliance circuit or a residential standby generator / transfer switch / interlock installation; Shape PHX records (e.g., CTR-102310087, CTR-102311225) show residential backup generators processed via Electronic Plan Review, but a written city policy page is needed to confirm.

Could not retrieve the full body text of Electric Vehicle Chargers – Residential Permitting (TRT/DOC/00311) at https://www.phoenix.gov/pddsite/Documents/TRT/dsd_trt_pdf_00311.pdf to verify whether all existing single-family Level 2 EVSE installations qualify for a Quick Permit or when plan review is triggered.
Could not find a published City of Phoenix master list of all eligible Residential Electrical Quick Permit scopes to confirm whether subpanels or standby generators qualify without plan review.

Could not verify the revision date printed on Electrical Submittal Requirements - Interpretation (TRT/DOC/00574) at https://www.phoenix.gov/content/dam/phoenix/pddsite/documents/trt/external/dsd_trt_pdf_00574.pdf.
No City of Phoenix-specific residential electrical load calculation worksheet or EV charger load factor percentage (100% vs 125%) was found on phoenix.gov.
